newsitem.title: USA: Trism sees $1-$2 mln charges for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Trism sees $1-$2 mln charges for 1997.

text.p: Trism Inc said a plan to consolidate management of its four business units is likely to result in about $1-$2 million in charges in one or more periods for 1997.
It said the charges would involve non-recurring reorganization, severance and related expenses.
Trism, a specialized trucking company, said its Secured, Heavy Haul, Transport and Logistics units are to be consolidated into a single administrative operation.

It said the reorganization aims to improve productivity and profitability by eliminating duplication, improving business systems, cutting managerial and administrative staff and implementing other cost-cutting measures.

"While Trism has enjoyed strong revenue growth, from $113 million at inception in 1990 to approximately $310 million in 1996, we recognize the need to create a more efficient cost structure, said chairman James Revie.
He said the goal of the reorganization is to cut operating expenses by approximately $4-$6 million on an annualized basis in 1997 and to reduce the "days outstanding" of accounts receivables.

On January 2, Trism said it expected to report a loss of approximately $0.35 a share for the fourth quarter ended December 31, 1996. The company said it expects its fourth quarter financial results to be line with that announcement, although its auditors, Coopers & Lybrand, have not yet complete the regular year-end audit.
It said it expects to report financial results for 1996 within the next few days upon completion of the audit.
